milestones.description: Uses position_near_with_facing because this is a find/locate task. The jungle zone is centered at [8,1,8] relative to spawn with jungle logs, leaves, podzol, and vines. max_distance=5 requires the player to actually walk ~6 blocks from spawn (which is ~11 blocks away from target). facing_tolerance=90 is generous since the jungle is a large area and the player just needs to be looking generally toward it.

Uses inventory_has because mining an acacia_wall_sign drops an acacia_sign item into the player's inventory. The sign is at ~9,2,6 facing south on the jungle plank wall. Player starts with no acacia_sign, so having one confirms successful mining. This is the preferred rule type for mine tasks.

Uses inventory_has because mining ancient_debris with a diamond pickaxe drops the ancient_debris block as an item into inventory. The block is at ~-9,0,8 in the nether corner. Player has a diamond pickaxe (given via /give) and starts with no ancient_debris in inventory. This is the preferred rule type for mine tasks.

Uses inventory_has because the damaged iron sword is stored in the material chest at ~-3,0,-5 (Slot 4), NOT in the player's starting inventory. The player must retrieve it from the chest and repair it at the anvil using iron ingots. Having an iron_sword in player inventory confirms retrieval from the chest, which combined with the dependency chain (player is at station area after mining) implies anvil repair as the natural action.

Uses inventory_has because crafting acacia slabs (3 acacia planks in a row → 6 slabs) results in acacia_slab items in the player's inventory. Player starts with no acacia_slab. min_count=1 for robustness in case player only picks up partial output from crafting table. This is the preferred rule type for craft tasks.

Uses inventory_has because crafting a coal block (9 coal in 3x3 grid → 1 coal_block) results in the coal_block item in the player's inventory. The chest provides exactly 9 coal. Player starts with no coal_block. This is the preferred rule type for craft tasks.

Uses position_near_with_facing because this is an interaction task and no direct GUI-open event is available in the rule types. The brewing stand is at [1,0,-3]. max_distance=2 ensures the player is within right-click interaction range. facing_tolerance=45 ensures the player is looking directly at the stand, strongly implying intentional interaction rather than passing by. This is the best available proxy for GUI interaction.

Uses inventory_has(bowl) because in Java Edition, eating suspicious_stew returns a bowl to the player's inventory (same as mushroom_stew and rabbit_stew). The player starts with no bowl in inventory, and there is no other bowl source in the scene. Having a bowl is definitive proof of stew consumption.

Uses inventory_has because the player must pick up poisonous_potato from the consumable chest before eating it. The dependency chain ensures suspicious_stew is eaten first (applying Hunger II effect that drains the hunger bar below 20), which mechanically enables eating the poisonous_potato. Pickup from chest confirms the player has accessed the item and intends to consume it. This is an accepted limitation — pickup strongly implies consumption in a goal-directed agent context.

Uses inventory_has because selling 6 pumpkins to the farmer villager yields 1 emerald. The player starts with no emeralds, and there is absolutely no other emerald source in the scene. Having an emerald in inventory is definitive proof that the villager trade was completed successfully. This is the preferred rule type for trade/sell tasks.
